title: microfeed documentation
excerpt: Publish a website, RSS feed, and JSON Feed from an open-source CMS in your own Cloudflare account.
content_html:
Publishblogs, podcasts, documents, video, audio, and curations
on your own domain
without managing servers

An agentic, lightweight, open-source CMS that runs in your Cloudflare account. Manage content through the Admin UI, CLI, WebMCP, or remote MCP server. Share it through your website, RSS, JSON Feed, and API.

Get startedView on GitHub

Open source

Own your code and your data. Deploy microfeed into your own Cloudflare account.

Serverless

Cloudflare Workers, D1, and optional R2 run the site without a server for you to patch or maintain.

Free-tier friendly

Many personal and small sites can stay within Cloudflare’s included usage. Check the current Workers, D1, and R2 allowances as your audience grows.

Headless

Manage content through the Admin UI, CLI, WebMCP, or remote MCP server. Connect AI assistants such as ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini with Streamable HTTP and OAuth, or build integrations with the API.

Features

  • Open distribution — Publish a website, RSS feed, and JSON Feed.
  • Media publishing — Share text, links, images, audio, video, and documents.
  • Admin UI — Create, edit, review, and publish content in the visual dashboard.
  • CLI — Run content commands from a terminal or local coding agent with browser-authorized access.
  • WebMCP — Let a compatible browser agent edit visible drafts with experimental dashboard tools.
  • MCP server — Give AI assistants remote content tools on each instance using Streamable HTTP and OAuth read/write permissions.
  • Themes and website code — Preview and activate theme versions or add shared HTML, CSS, and JavaScript as a site owner.
  • Theme development — Build, validate, preview, and release a standalone theme package.
  • Site access — Choose Public, Headless, or Offline delivery without deleting content.
  • Content automation — Choose MCP, the API, webhooks, or the content CLI and explore practical automation examples.
  • Admin API — Read or change content with named keys and an instance-generated contract.
  • Webhooks and integrations — Receive signed notifications whenever subscribed content changes.
  • Site management — Update, inspect, snapshot, and migrate an instance safely.
